title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 8

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the fault-report demonstration take place?
tasks.audioText: The electronics tutor will demonstrate how to describe a fault in a training circuit on Wednesday at one. Students should bring the fault-report template and the circuit diagram. The tutor will focus on observations, test conditions and evidence. Students will not repair or energise any equipment during this classroom activity.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which two documents should students bring?
tasks.audioText: The electronics tutor will demonstrate how to describe a fault in a training circuit on Wednesday at one. Students should bring the fault-report template and the circuit diagram. The tutor will focus on observations, test conditions and evidence. Students will not repair or energise any equipment during this classroom activity.
options: The fault-report template and circuit diagram

tasks.prompt: A trainee reported that an indicator lamp did not light when the training board was examined. The report identified the board reference and described the observation. It also stated that the supply status had not yet been confirmed. The trainee avoided claiming that the lamp itself was defective because the available information was not enough to identify the cause. Reading 1. What did the trainee observe?
options: The indicator lamp did not light

tasks.prompt: Why did the trainee avoid naming the lamp as defective?
options: There was not enough information to identify the cause

tasks.prompt: The cause of the fault ___ confirmed at the time of the report.
Choose TWO elements of a useful troubleshooting report.
options: A guessed cause presented as fact

tasks.prompt: A visible or measurable sign of a problem is a ___.
You have only observed a symptom and do not know the cause. What should you write?
options: The power supply is definitely faulty.
The indicator did not light during the observation; the cause has not been confirmed.
I will state a cause to complete the form.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of electronic troubleshooting reports in a logical order.
options: Record the conditions and available evidence
correctOrder: Record the conditions and available evidence

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words describing an electronic fault for a report. Separate the observed symptom from a possible cause and include the equipment reference.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the report identifies the equipment and describes the observed symptom (0–2); it separates the symptom from a possible cause and avoids presenting an unconfirmed diagnosis as fact (0–2); the report is concise and logically organised with understandable grammar (0–2); fault/equipment-reference vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
